sections.sectionSummaryBrief: Just as there are infinite levels in Torah study, so too in the performance and intention of mitzvos, explaining the varying garments made for the soul in the lower and upper Gan Eden.

translations.translation: And behold, just as in the study of Torah
(even in the revealed aspect of Torah,
and certainly in the inner aspect of Torah)
there is a multitude of levels without end,
so too is it in the fulfillment of the mitzvos,
even in the action of the mitzvos and certainly in the intention of the mitzvos,
that there is a multitude of levels.
And based on this, one will understand what is known,
that from the action of the mitzvos, garments are made for the soul in the lower Gan Eden, and from the intention of the mitzvos, garments are made in the upper Gan Eden,
for at first glance,
behold, even in the lower Gan Eden itself,
and likewise in the upper Gan Eden itself,
there is a multitude of levels,
and how is it possible that in all the levels there would be the same garments?
And the explanation of this is,
that in the action of the mitzvos and likewise in the intention of the mitzvos there is a multitude of levels as mentioned above.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: Even though the intention of a mitzvah is its soul, many aspects of intention are also in the revealed Torah, and just as one asks to see wonders from the Torah's body and garment, so too must the wonders of mitzvah intentions be seen from the simple intentions.

translations.translation: And behold, although the intention of the mitzvah is the soul of the mitzvah, which generally belongs to the soul of the Torah,
nevertheless,
many matters of the intention of the mitzvos are also in the revealed aspect of Torah.
Both regarding the general intention
of mitzvos
(that is common to all mitzvos equally)
to fulfill the will of G-d — for this intention is also according to the revealed aspect of Torah
(except that through the study of the inner aspect of Torah,
the intention and will of the person to fulfill the will of G-d is in a more elevated manner),
and also the particular intentions
that are in each specific mitzvah,
behold, the reason and intention of many mitzvos is also explained in the revealed aspect of Torah,
even according to the simple approach
[to the extent that the reason for many mitzvos is explicit in the verse],
and certainly according to the way of Remez and Drush,
except that the reason and intention of the mitzvos according to the way of Sod
(the inner aspect of Torah)
is much more elevated,
and through this, depth etc. is added also to the reason according to the revealed aspect.
And it can be said,
that just as regarding the seeing of the wonders of Torah,
the request "Open my eyes and I will behold wonders from Your Torah" is that the seeing of the wonders of Torah
(the soul and the soul of the soul)
should be from Your Torah,
from those matters that are in the revealed aspect of Torah,
from the body of Torah and also from the garment of Torah
(as above in section 4),
so too is it regarding the intention of the mitzvos,
that the wonders of the intention of the mitzvos
[the intentions of the AriZal,
and higher than that]
must be seen from within the intentions according to the simple approach,
and moreover — from within the intentions according to the simple approach that are understood by a five-year-old studying Scripture
[which are analogous to the garment of Torah,
the narratives of Torah,
which even young children learn].

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This matter of knowing the most elevated concepts from their simple aspects applies even more to mitzvos and prayer, explaining why the Tzemach Tzedek cited "I pray with the knowledge of this child" in his discourse on the root of the mitzvah of prayer.

translations.translation: And to add,
regarding the intention of the mitzvos,
this matter applies
[that the most elevated matters should be known from those matters as they are simply]
even more so than regarding Torah.
For the advantage in this, that the knowledge of the wonders is from the matters that are in simplicity, is that through this the person's knowledge of the wonders will also be from his own aspect
(as above in section 4),
and since the purpose of the mitzvos is to refine the creations through them
(as above in section 5),
to effect clarification and refinement in the person who fulfills the mitzvah,
[for the primary clarification and refinement is through the intention of the mitzvos,
and the more elevated the intention is,
the more elevated the clarification and refinement is],
therefore,
regarding the matter of mitzvos it applies even more that the knowledge of the wonders of the intention of the mitzvos should be from within the intentions that are in simplicity.
And based on this, one can explain what the Tzemach Tzedek brings in the discourse "The Root of the Mitzvah of Prayer"
the phrase "I pray with the knowledge of this child."
For at first glance,
in the discourse "The Root of the Mitzvah of Prayer" he explains the matter of prayer
[in general,
and also several particular matters of prayer]
according to Kabbalah,
and even more — according to Chassidus,
and what place is there in this discourse to bring the matter of "I pray with the knowledge of this child"?
And it can be said,
that in this he hints,
that the intentions of prayer in the most elevated levels must be connected with the matter of prayer as it is according to the knowledge of a child,
both regarding the general matter of prayer — that the knowledge of the matter of prayer in the most elevated levels should also be from the matter of prayer as a child understands it,
and also regarding the explanation of the matters
(the verses,
requests, etc.)
that are said in prayer,
that the most elevated explanations must be in accordance with
[to the extent that their knowledge should be from within]
the simple meaning of the words of prayer as a child understands them.
And although this matter applies to all matters in Torah,
nevertheless,
since the matter of prayer is an elevation from below to above,
clarification and refinement of the person,
therefore in prayer this matter applies more
(in the manner explained above regarding mitzvos).
And therefore,
in the discourse "The Root of the Mitzvah of Prayer" the matter of "I pray with the knowledge of this child" is brought.
